name: City Centre and the Castle Quarter
tagline: Victorian arcades, the castle and everything on foot
description: Cardiff's centre packs the castle, the Principality Stadium and seven Victorian shopping arcades into a few walkable blocks. The arcades hold independent coffee roasters, record shops and small restaurants, while modern apartment blocks sit around the edges. Central station puts the whole of south Wales within reach.
bestFor: Short-stay nomads who want zero commute and trains on the doorstep
pros: Walk to cafes, gyms, coworking and the station
Victorian arcades give real independent coffee options
Bute Park is a two minute walk from the castle
cons: Rowdy and packed on match days at the stadium
Traffic and night noise around the main streets
Newer flats charge a premium for small floorplans

name: Cardiff Bay
tagline: Waterfront apartments, the Senedd and sunset walks
description: Cardiff Bay is the redeveloped docklands two miles south of the centre, built around Mermaid Quay, the Wales Millennium Centre and the Senedd. Modern apartment blocks line the water, the barrage gives a long flat walking route, and restaurants and bars face the marina.
bestFor: Remote workers who want a modern flat with a water view and running routes
pros: Newer apartments with good broadband and balconies
Barrage and waterfront path for daily exercise
Concerts, theatre and restaurants at Mermaid Quay
cons: A 35 minute walk or short train ride from the centre
Exposed and windy off the water in winter

name: Pontcanna
tagline: Tree-lined Victorian streets and Cardiff's best brunch
description: Pontcanna is the leafy district west of the river, with wide Victorian terraces, Llandaff Fields and Pontcanna Fields on its edge, and a run of delis, brunch spots and independent shops along Kings Road and Pontcanna Street. It draws media types, families and anyone who works from a cafe.
bestFor: Nomads staying a while who want green space, good coffee and a settled neighbourhood
pros: Huge green fields and the Taff trail on the doorstep
Best independent cafe and deli cluster in Cardiff
Quiet residential streets, 20 minute walk to town
cons: The most expensive rents outside the Bay

name: Cathays
tagline: Student Cardiff, cheap rent and late-night takeaways
description: Cathays sits between the university buildings and the centre, a dense grid of red-brick terraces where most of Cardiff's students live. Salisbury Road and Woodville Road carry the cheap eats, bubble tea and pubs, and Cathays train station is one stop from the centre. Rents are the lowest of any central option.
bestFor: Budget nomads happy to trade quiet for the cheapest central rent in the city
pros: Cheapest rooms and flats within walking distance of town
Train station one stop from Cardiff Central
Cheap food and cafes open late
cons: Noisy student streets, especially midweek nights
Housing stock is worn and often poorly insulated
Empties out and feels dead over the summer

name: Roath
tagline: Lake, park and the Wellfield Road cafe strip
description: Roath wraps around Roath Park and its lake, mixing large Victorian houses with terraced streets. Wellfield Road and Albany Road supply the independent cafes, bakeries and pubs, and the park has a boating lake, botanical gardens and a long walking loop. It sits between student Cathays and quieter family streets.
bestFor: Nomads who want a real neighbourhood with a park, cafes and moderate rent
pros: Roath Park lake and gardens for daily walks
Strong independent cafe and pub scene on Wellfield Road
Cheaper than Pontcanna for similar Victorian housing
cons: No train station, so buses or a 30 minute walk to town
Streets nearer Cathays get student noise
Older terraces can be damp and draughty in winter
